judged_text: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when the base assignment produced null (neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists), discarding every collected team calendar. A collective booking whose organizer has no calendar connected but whose team members do keeps evt.destinationCalendar null, so EventManager takes the create-in-organizer-credentials fallback and the members' calendars get nothing — the multi-host feature silently does nothing for exactly the mixed-configuration teams it targets.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [..] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [..] : null` (so it can be `null`). Immediately after, for collective team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If the organizer has no destination calendar and the event type also has none, `evt.destinationCalendar` stays `null` and the optional-chained `push` is a no-op, discarding all collected `teamDestinationCalendars`. This is directly verifiable from the diff and can cause collective events to miss creating events on team members’ calendars in that mixed configuration.
